frozen_original.synopsis: White House advisor Stephen Miller drafted the detailed implementation plans for Schedule F civil service reclassification, compiled and maintained enemies lists of government officials and perceived critics targeted for removal or investigation, and designed the loyalty purge mechanisms used to systematically eliminate nonpartisan career employees from the federal workforce. Miller's enemies lists reportedly included hundreds of government employees, journalists, academics, and political figures. The combination of Schedule F implementation and targeted lists created the infrastructure for a comprehensive authoritarian capture of the executive branch.

primary.title: Trump Reinstates Schedule F as Schedule Policy/Career
primary.description_short: Trump's January 20, 2025 executive order reinstated Schedule F under the name Schedule Policy/Career.
primary.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Donald Trump signed an executive order immediately reinstating the 2020 Schedule F order and renaming the category “Schedule Policy/Career.” The order directed the Office of Personnel Management to amend regulations and issue guidance on additional positions for agencies to consider. It establishes a federal workforce policy directive; it does not show how many employees were later reclassified or removed.
primary.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed “Restoring Accountability to Policy-Influencing Positions Within the Federal Workforce.” Section 2 immediately reinstated Executive Order 13957, the 2020 order creating Schedule F, subject to amendments in the new order. Those amendments replaced the excepted-service schedule label “F” with “Policy/Career” and directed the Office of Personnel Management to amend regulations that could impede implementation. The order also directed OPM to issue, within 30 days, guidance about additional position categories agencies should consider recommending for inclusion. It says employees in or applicants for these positions need not personally or politically support the President, but are required to faithfully implement administration policies; failure to do so is grounds for dismissal. These are the signed order’s rules and directions. The accessed document does not establish how many positions were later reclassified, how many employees lost protections, or whether any specific person was dismissed under it. This record describes the enacted policy mechanism, not a completed workforce purge or an asserted list of political enemies.

corrected_proposal.title: Trump Reinstates Schedule F as Schedule Policy/Career
corrected_proposal.description_short: Trump's January 20, 2025 executive order reinstated Schedule F under the name Schedule Policy/Career.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Donald Trump signed an executive order immediately reinstating the 2020 Schedule F order and renaming the category “Schedule Policy/Career.” The order directed the Office of Personnel Management to amend regulations and issue guidance on additional positions for agencies to consider. It establishes a federal workforce policy directive; it does not show how many employees were later reclassified or removed.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed “Restoring Accountability to Policy-Influencing Positions Within the Federal Workforce.” Section 2 immediately reinstated Executive Order 13957, the 2020 order creating Schedule F, subject to amendments in the new order. Those amendments replaced the excepted-service schedule label “F” with “Policy/Career” and directed the Office of Personnel Management to amend regulations that could impede implementation. The order also directed OPM to issue, within 30 days, guidance about additional position categories agencies should consider recommending for inclusion. It says employees in or applicants for these positions need not personally or politically support the President, but are required to faithfully implement administration policies; failure to do so is grounds for dismissal. These are the signed order’s rules and directions. The accessed document does not establish how many positions were later reclassified, how many employees lost protections, or whether any specific person was dismissed under it. This record describes the enacted policy mechanism, not a completed workforce purge or an asserted list of political enemies.

frozen_original.title: Trump executive order allowing prosecution of critics for material support of terrorism
frozen_original.synopsis: Trump signed an executive order that could allow the prosecution of domestic critics and activists under material support for terrorism statutes, effectively criminalizing political dissent. The order broadly expanded the definition of material support to potentially include speech, donations, and association with organizations designated as terrorist-adjacent by the administration. Civil liberties advocates warned the order could be used to prosecute anyone who donated to or participated in protests organized by groups the administration had targeted.
